record.original_question: Is the regular order of contact of a smooth pseudoconvex domain the same as the commutator type, one vector field at a time.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.4.1 Is the regular order of contact of a smooth pseudoconvex domain the same as the commutator type, one vector field at a time. -J. McNeal, mcneal@math.princeton.edu

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smooth pseudoconvex domain with defining function $r$, and let $p \in \partial\Omega$ be a boundary point. Denote by $T^{1,0}\partial\Omega$ the holomorphic tangent bundle of $\partial\Omega$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the Levi form of $\partial\Omega$.

For a smooth $(1,0)$ vector field $L$ tangent to $\partial\Omega$ near $p$, define:

(i) The regular order of contact of $L$ at $p$ as the maximal order of vanishing at $p$ of $r \circ \gamma$ over all smooth holomorphic curves $\gamma:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,p)$ whose tangent at $0$ is a nonzero multiple of $L(p)$ (equivalently, the order of contact of one-dimensional complex varieties tangent to $L$ with $\partial\Omega$ at $p$).

(ii) The commutator type (Hörmander/Bloom type) of $L$ at $p$ as the smallest integer $m \geq 2$ such that some iterated commutator of length $m$ formed from $L$, $\bar L$, and their conjugates, evaluated at $p$, has nonzero component in the direction transverse to the maximal complex tangent space (equivalently, applies a nonzero pairing with $\partial r$).

Question: For every smooth pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$, every boundary point $p \in \partial\Omega$, and every smooth $(1,0)$ tangent vector field $L$ near $p$ with $L(p)\neq 0$, is the regular order of contact of $L$ at $p$ equal to the commutator type of $L$ at $p$?
artifact.category_tag: finite type in several complex variables
artifact.status_search_result: This is the single-vector-field case of Bloom's conjecture on the equality of commutator type, Levi form type, and regular order of contact for smooth pseudoconvex hypersurfaces. Bloom (1981) proved equality of Levi-form type and regular contact type. The full conjecture, including equality with the commutator type, was settled in complex dimension three by Huang and Yin (2021), but remains open in complex dimensions $n \geq 4$; further partial progress (Huang–Yin and others, 2023–2025) treats certain multi-type and Levi-type analogues.

status_evidence.title: Regular multi-types and the Bloom conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The commutator type, the regular contact type and the Levi form type are the same for a smooth pseudoconvex real hypersurface; in complex dimension three this provides a complete solution of a long standing conjecture of Bloom.
status_evidence.claim: The single-vector-field equality is solved in complex dimension three.

status_evidence.title: Commutator type and Levi type of a system of CR vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: The commutator type and the Levi type associated with a subbundle of the CR tangent vector bundle are the same when either of them is less than 8...
status_evidence.claim: Partial results in higher dimensions; full conjecture remains open in dimension at least 4.

status_evidence.title: Regular Versus Singular Order of Contact on Pseudoconvex Hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the relationship between regular and singular orders of contact on pseudoconvex hypersurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Active area; equality of various type notions remains a focus of research.
